scenes.sub: The cash flow trap nobody talks about
scenes.line: How can a company that makes a profit still go bankrupt? Let us understand the cash flow trap.

scenes.say: Record sales this year! We made *₹50 Cr* profit!
scenes.line: Meet Mr. Mehta. His company just reported record sales and fifty crore rupees of profit.

scenes.say: Then why can't you pay *salaries* next month?
scenes.line: So why can he not pay salaries next month? Because profit is an opinion, but cash is a fact.

scenes.title: Profit went *up*... cash went *down*
scenes.line: His customers pay after one hundred and twenty days, but suppliers want money in thirty. Cash kept falling every quarter.

scenes.title: 3 warning signs to check
scenes.line: Watch three warning signs. Rising receivable days, piling inventory, and negative operating cash flow despite profit.

scenes.text: Revenue is vanity, profit is sanity, but *cash is king*.
scenes.line: Remember. Revenue is vanity, profit is sanity, but cash is king.

titles: Why Profitable Companies Go Bankrupt | Cash Flow Explained Simply
Profit ≠ Cash: The Trap That Kills Businesses
